Definition: properly, to scrutinize, i.e. look intently at; hence (with recognition implied), to acknowledge, be acquainted with, care for, respect, revere, or (with suspicion implied), to disregard, ignore, be strange toward, reject, resign, dissimulate (as if ignorant or disowning)
BiblicalUsage: Nakar means to recognise or discern, to know again what was hidden, and it turns on a coat, a blessing, and a face. In Genesis 27:23 Isaac discerns Jacob not, because his hands are hairy like Esau's, so he blesses him, and in Genesis 37:33 Jacob knows the coat and says, it is my son's coat, and Joseph is without doubt rent in pieces. In Deuteronomy 33:9 Levi says of his father and mother, I have not seen him, and does not acknowledge his brethren, and in 1 Kings 20:41 the king of Israel discerns the prophet when he takes the ashes away from his face.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe recognition is the hinge of so many stories, because Isaac failed to discern and blessed the wrong son, and Jacob recognised a coat and believed a lie. The same word covers the prophet recognised too late, and I hold that the danger is not in seeing but in seeing what we want to see.
